title: OperationEvent
description: Event emitted by the client core for GUI/CLI (SPRUT-CLIENT-SPECIFICATION 7.1 item 4, 8.1). In `sprut --json` long operations write one event per line (JSON Lines) to stdout; stdout carries nothing but these events (and the single result object of short commands): child processes never inherit the CLI's stdout, their output goes to the technical log. Optional members are omitted when absent; null is never used. In every event, progress.current <= progress.total when both are present. PRODUCER conformance: an emitted event matches this schema exactly (no other members); reason_code is in registry/reason-codes.json; operation is a registered operation kind and state is a state of its machine (operation_kinds in registry/state-machines.json). CONSUMER behaviour: a consumer first drops members it does not know (top level and inside progress; later minor versions may add optional members within the same schema_version), then validates against this schema; it accepts well-formed reason codes, operations and states missing from its copy of the registries (newer contracts) and treats an unknown reason code as a generic error (CLI exit code fallback 1). A line that fails validation is reported as a diagnostic (stderr or log), never silently dropped. Consumers never derive readiness or consent from the event stream alone: the BootstrapJournal and a fresh probe are authoritative. Any member that changes a security or consent decision requires a new schema_version, never a minor addition. Everything else that fails this schema is rejected by both.

schema_version.description: Major version of the event format. A consumer rejects an unknown value; 1.0 is not 1 (type integer).

type.description: progress: work advanced within the current state; state: the operation entered `state`; result: final outcome of the operation; error: the operation failed or needs action, reason_code is required.

operation_id.description: Identifier of the operation (CF01). Opaque to consumers.

operation.description: Operation kind from operation_kinds in registry/state-machines.json (e.g. bootstrap, node_status, model_pull, mode_switch); it selects the lifecycle machine whose states `state` uses (bootstrap, node_status or the generic task). Required: an operation kind that is not registered cannot emit events until it is added here.

state.description: Current state of the operation, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; a state of the machine that operation_kinds maps `operation` to. Always interpreted together with `operation`.

reason_code.description: Code from registry/reason-codes.json. Required for type=error; may accompany other types (e.g. state ACTION_REQUIRED).

message.description: Human-readable text authored by the client in its UI language (never raw subprocess output). At most 1024 Unicode code points (not UTF-16 units: Java must count with String.codePointCount), no control characters (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F), no zero-width or BOM characters (U+200B-U+200F, U+FEFF), no line/paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029) and no bidi embedding/override/isolate controls (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069). Not for machine parsing; may be empty. Must not contain secrets.

ts.description: Event time, RFC 3339 in UTC with the `Z` suffix, seconds 00-59 and 0-9 fractional second digits, e.g. 2026-11-06T10:15:30.123Z.

progress.description: Optional progress within the current state.

total.description: Omitted when unknown. When present, current <= total (checked outside JSON Schema).

unit.description: Unit of current/total, lower_snake_case, e.g. bytes, steps, items.

step.description: Identifier of the plan step or sub-step being executed; client-authored, 1-128 code points, the same forbidden characters as message.
